locations.title: Google Chrome data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Chrome profiles: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, extensions and site data. Removing it signs you out everywhere in Chrome and loses anything not synced to your Google account. To free space, use Delete browsing data in Chrome's settings.

locations.title: Google Chrome data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Chrome profiles: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, extensions and site data. Removing it signs you out everywhere in Chrome and loses anything not synced to your Google account. To free space, use Delete browsing data in Chrome's settings.

locations.title: Google Chrome data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Chrome profiles: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, extensions and site data. Removing it signs you out everywhere in Chrome and loses anything not synced to your Google account. To free space, use Delete browsing data in Chrome's settings.

locations.title: Google software updater
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Google's background updater for Chrome and other Google apps, including update files it downloaded. It reinstalls itself the next time a Google app updates.

locations.title: Microsoft Edge data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Edge profiles: favorites, history, saved passwords, extensions and site data. Removing it signs you out everywhere in Edge. To free space, clear browsing data in Edge's settings.

locations.title: Brave browser data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Brave profiles: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, extensions and site data. To free space, clear browsing data in Brave's settings.

locations.title: Arc browser data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Arc spaces, tabs, history, passwords and site data. To free space, clear browsing data in Arc's settings.

locations.title: Firefox profiles
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your Firefox profiles: bookmarks, history, saved passwords, add-ons and site data. To free space, clear history and site data in Firefox's settings.

locations.title: Slack data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Slack's local copy of your workspaces, messages and files. Removing it signs you out; Slack downloads your messages again after you sign back in. To free space, use Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart in Slack.

locations.title: Discord data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Discord's settings, sign-in and cached media. Removing it signs you out of Discord; it downloads what it needs again.

locations.title: Microsoft Teams data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Teams' sign-in, settings and cached chats and files. Removing it signs you out of Teams; it downloads your chats again.

locations.title: Microsoft Office shared data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, templates, fonts, Outlook mail and cached documents shared by Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook. Removing it can reset Office or lose documents that haven't synced yet.

locations.title: Webex data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Messages, meeting files and caches stored by Cisco Webex. If you still use Webex, leave it; if you don't, uninstall Webex and this can go with it.

locations.title: Zoom data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Zoom's settings, chat history and downloaded components. Removing it resets Zoom.

locations.title: Zoom recordings
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Meetings you recorded with Zoom. Delete recordings you no longer need in Finder.

locations.title: Spotify data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Spotify's settings, sign-in and offline music. Downloaded songs can be removed from inside Spotify.

locations.title: Adobe app data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, presets, fonts and caches for Adobe apps such as Photoshop, Premiere Pro and Lightroom. Clear media caches from each app's preferences rather than removing this folder.

locations.title: Adobe media cache
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Preview and audio files Premiere Pro, After Effects and Audition create for faster playback. Fine to remove with those apps closed; they rebuild previews as needed.

locations.title: JetBrains IDE settings
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings and plugins for JetBrains IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm or WebStorm. Old version folders can be removed with JetBrains Toolbox; the current ones hold your settings.

locations.title: Docker Desktop data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Docker's images, containers and volumes, which can include local databases. Removing this deletes all of them; clean up from Docker Desktop (Troubleshoot > Clean / Purge data) or run `docker system prune` in Terminal.

locations.title: Ollama
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings and keys for Ollama, the tool for running AI models locally.

locations.title: Ollama AI models
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: AI models you downloaded with Ollama. Remove the ones you don't use with `ollama rm <name>`; you can download them again with `ollama pull`.

locations.title: LM Studio
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings and chats for LM Studio, the app for running AI models locally.

locations.title: LM Studio AI models
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: AI models you downloaded in LM Studio. Remove ones you don't use from LM Studio's My Models page; you can download them again any time.

locations.title: Hugging Face model downloads
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: AI models and datasets downloaded by Hugging Face tools. They download again when code uses them, which can take a while for large models.

locations.title: Conda Python installation
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: A Python distribution with its packages and environments. Removing it breaks projects that use it. To free space, run `conda clean --all` or remove environments you don't use with `conda env remove`.

locations.title: Conda package downloads
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Package files conda keeps after installing them. `conda clean --all` removes them safely; your environments keep working.

locations.title: Python versions (pyenv)
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Python versions installed with pyenv. Remove versions you don't use with `pyenv uninstall <version>`.

locations.title: Node.js versions (nvm)
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Node.js versions installed with nvm, with their global packages. Remove versions you don't use with `nvm uninstall <version>`.

locations.title: Rust toolchains (rustup)
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Rust compilers installed with rustup. Remove toolchains you don't use with `rustup toolchain uninstall <name>`.

locations.title: Rust tools (Cargo)
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Command-line tools installed with Cargo plus its settings. Its download cache (registry) is listed separately and can go.

locations.title: Go module cache
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Downloaded Go modules and build cache. `go clean -modcache` removes them safely; Go downloads modules again on the next build.

locations.title: Go workspace
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Go tools you installed and downloaded modules. Your own Go projects may live here too.

locations.title: Gradle data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Gradle settings and downloaded libraries. The caches inside are listed separately and can go.

locations.title: Maven repository
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Java libraries downloaded by Maven. They download again on the next build.

locations.title: Android SDK
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Android build tools, platforms and emulator images used by Android Studio. Remove versions you don't need in Android Studio's SDK Manager.

locations.title: Android emulators
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Virtual Android devices and their data. Delete ones you don't use in Android Studio's Device Manager.

locations.title: Android tools settings
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, debug keys and emulator data for Android tools.

locations.title: Unity data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, downloaded packages and caches for the Unity game engine. Manage installed editor versions in Unity Hub.

locations.title: Unity cache
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Downloaded Unity packages and Asset Store files. Unity downloads them again when a project needs them.

locations.title: Parallels virtual machines
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Virtual machines and everything installed and saved inside them. Removing one erases that machine; delete ones you no longer need from Parallels Desktop's Control Center.

locations.title: UTM virtual machines
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Virtual machines created in UTM and everything saved inside them. Delete ones you no longer need from inside UTM.

locations.title: VMware virtual machines
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: VMware Fusion virtual machines and everything saved inside them. Delete ones you no longer need from VMware Fusion.

locations.title: Steam games
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Games installed through Steam and their saves. Uninstall games you don't play from your Steam library (right-click a game > Manage > Uninstall).

locations.title: Dropbox files
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Files synced with Dropbox. Deleting them here deletes them from Dropbox and your other devices too. To free space, make files online-only in Dropbox instead.

locations.title: OneDrive files
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Files synced with OneDrive. Deleting them here deletes them from OneDrive and your other devices too. To free space, use Free up space (online-only) in OneDrive instead.

locations.title: Google Drive files
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Files synced with Google Drive and its local cache. Deleting files here deletes them from Google Drive too. To free space, switch Google Drive to streaming files instead of mirroring them.

locations.title: Box files
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Files synced with Box. Deleting them here deletes them from Box too.

locations.title: iCloud Drive
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Files in iCloud Drive. To free space, turn on Optimize Mac Storage in System Settings > Apple Account > iCloud > iCloud Drive.

locations.title: Messages attachments
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Photos, videos and files from your conversations. Remove large attachments in System Settings > General > Storage > Messages, or set Messages to keep messages for a shorter time.

locations.title: Mail data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Your downloaded email and attachments. Manage it in the Mail app; deleting files here can corrupt your mailboxes.

locations.title: Claude app data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, sign-in and local data for the Claude desktop app. Removing it signs you out of Claude and resets the app.

locations.title: Claude virtual machine
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: The Linux virtual machine the Claude app uses to run tasks on your Mac. Claude downloads it again the next time it needs it, which can take a while.

locations.title: Claude agent session files
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Working files from past Claude agent sessions on this Mac. Check that nothing in them is still needed before removing them.

locations.title: Claude Code settings and history
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, plugins, memory and conversation history for the Claude Code command-line tool.

locations.title: Claude Code installation
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Installed versions of the Claude Code command-line tool. Only the newest is used; Claude Code cleans up older versions itself as it updates.

locations.title: Codex settings and history
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings, sessions and logs for OpenAI's Codex command-line tool.

locations.title: Codex runtime downloads
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Runtimes and dependencies the Codex tool downloaded to run code. It downloads them again when needed.

locations.title: VS Code app data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: VS Code's settings, workspace history and extension data. Its caches are listed separately and can go.

locations.title: VS Code extensions
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Extensions you installed in VS Code. Removing them uninstalls them; manage extensions in VS Code's Extensions view (old versions are cleaned up automatically).

locations.title: Cursor app data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Cursor's settings, extensions and workspace history. Its caches are listed separately and can go.

locations.title: Fly.io command-line tool
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: The flyctl tool and your Fly.io sign-in. Removing it signs you out of Fly.io on this Mac.

locations.title: Supabase CLI
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Settings and sign-in for the Supabase command-line tool. Local Supabase databases live in Docker; stop them with `supabase stop`.

locations.title: Xcode data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Xcode's settings, archives and caches. The parts that can go (build data, device support, previews) are listed separately.

locations.title: Xcode coding assistant data
locations.label: review
locations.explanation: Components and data for Xcode's coding assistant, including AI agents it downloaded. Xcode can download them again when you use the assistant.

locations.title: Simulator data
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: iOS Simulator devices and runtimes. Delete simulators you don't use in Xcode (Window > Devices and Simulators).

locations.title: Homebrew
locations.label: keep
locations.explanation: Command-line tools installed with Homebrew. Run `brew cleanup` to remove old versions.

fileTypes.title: AI model
fileTypes.label: review
fileTypes.explanation: A downloaded AI model. Remove it if you no longer use the app or tool that needs it; it can be downloaded again.

fileTypes.title: Disk image
fileTypes.label: review
fileTypes.explanation: A disk image. If you've already installed or copied what's inside, it can go.

fileTypes.title: Installer package
fileTypes.label: review
fileTypes.explanation: An installer. Once the software is installed, the installer itself isn't needed.

fileTypes.title: Archive
fileTypes.label: review
fileTypes.explanation: A compressed archive. If you've already extracted what you need from it, it can go.

fileTypes.title: Virtual machine
fileTypes.label: review
fileTypes.explanation: A virtual machine or its disk. Removing it erases everything saved inside that virtual machine.

fileTypes.title: Database
fileTypes.label: keep
fileTypes.explanation: A database or data file. Removing it can lose the data an app or project keeps in it.
